name: maybe_Data_GetFirstRowC

name: maybe_Field_GetActiveSubObject

name: maybe_Field_MoveOverride_TestActorPosition

The sibling 0x0062DF2C is called with ((*0x007BE300)->f_08)->f_4C, which the established facts identify as the actor move-override table, so the query is a move-override area test; the table owner is still not proven.

Its single caller Field_NpcAction_UpdateMoveAndStuckCheck passes ((*0x007BE300)->f_08)->f_4C, the actor move-override table from the established facts; the entry layout is still only partly understood.

name: maybe_Actor_FindByField28

name: maybe_Ui_PokerWindow_GetRowValue

name: maybe_Field_Actor_CanPlaceAtCell

name: maybe_Party_LevelGapExceedsTwo

name: maybe_Ui_BagList_SetLabel

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_TargetGroup_ScaleBounds

The direction/mask arguments are still only partly understood, so the name stays generic.

name: maybe_Gfx_Atlas_FindPageForSize

name: maybe_Ui_CursorIcon_Close

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ApplyParam
summary: Applies a value to a scene object: refreshes the fade range through Model_Attach_SetFadeRange when the object has a valid handle, forwards the value to the object's vtable slot +0x84 if its +0x51 byte is clear, then calls 0x005F6000 with the value.
evidence: Same handle/fade prefix as 0x0018193C and the callees Model_Attach_SetFadeRange / Gfx_Model_AttachGadgetMesh are named, but the meaning of the forwarded value is still unknown and there are no callers.

name: Field_Action_Nut_Update
summary: Command handler (command 8) for the 'Nut' field action: when the world action flag is clear it resets f_31/f_2C, matches the owner node name against a 5-byte literal and 'Nut_1', and on the second match plays the follow-up animation; with the flag set it re-arms the 120..210 frame timer from the game RNG into f_2C.
evidence: The 'Nut_1' literal at 0x002C1114 is verified in code.bin and the sibling constructor 0x001BA4D4 installs g_fieldActionNutVtable, so the Nut-action identity is solid; the callees Anim_PlayByNameIfPresent, Field_SceneNode_TickChildren and Os_GetGameWork are all named.

name: maybe_Anim_PlayByNameB
summary: Plays the field-actor animation named by g_007A3C6C[actor->f_313] with an entry-0 fallback, fixes the height through 0x0066A244/0x005F7784 and clears three bytes at f_160+0x550..0x556.
evidence: The body is literally identical to 0x00182A28 (same table, f_313, f_374 height fix, cleared bytes) and still carries in_fpscr/in_s0 artefacts, so it stays a duplicate maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Action_CreateDig
summary: Minimal action-subclass constructor: runs Action_CtorBase and installs vtable 0x007595D0; the paired start routine is 0x001BA3F4.
evidence: The body is a bare vtable store and the attributed caller 0x0022E494 is a mixed 4 KB chunk, so the 'Dig' identity is still unproven.

name: maybe_Field_Action_CreateNut
summary: Minimal action-subclass constructor: runs Action_CtorBase and installs vtable 0x00759604 (the table right after the Dig action's), with handlers at 0x001BA510 and 0x001BA5D0.
evidence: Nothing in the body distinguishes it from the Dig factory except the vtable constant, and the attributed caller 0x0022E494 is an unreliable mixed Thumb chunk; the Nut identity is supported indirectly by the 'Nut_1' literal used in 0x002C1008.

name: Menu_UpdateItemIcon
signature: void Menu_UpdateItemIcon(void* menu, u32 actorId, u32 slot, u32 index)
summary: Refreshes one item icon/slot record of a menu page: walks the menu's five-slot id chain (+0x4E/+0x8E/+0xCE/+0x10E/+0x14E), builds the icon name from the inline 'it_0001' sheet literal and rebuilds the slot record through Menu_ItemIcon_LoadPack / Menu_IconModel_Release.
evidence: Both icon helpers are named menu icon routines (Menu_ItemIcon_LoadPack, Menu_IconModel_Release) and the caller Menu_Slot_StoreActorId is the slot-claim path, which pins the item-icon refresh; only an in_r12 artefact remains.

name: Menu_UpdateSkillIcon
signature: void Menu_UpdateSkillIcon(void* menu, u32 actorId, u32 skillId, u32 slot)
summary: Refreshes a skill icon/command entry: builds the skill icon name from the inline 'sk_0155'/'sk_0034'/'sk_0104' sheet literals and updates the five-slot id chain (+0x4D/+0x8D/+0xCD/+0x10D/+0x14D) and the slot record through Menu_SkillIcon_LoadPack / Menu_IconModel_Release.
evidence: The named callee Menu_SkillIcon_LoadPack is the skill counterpart of Menu_ItemIcon_LoadPack used by the now-confirmed item-icon twin 0x0020BC04, and the body is the same five-slot refresh with a different sheet prefix.

name: maybe_Ui_SingleLayoutObject_Dtor
summary: Small deleting destructor: releases the one embedded layout arena at +0x4C, runs the base destructor and frees the object; the body is identical to maybe_Ui_WidgetWithSubObject_DeletingDtor (0x002BD834), a template copy.
evidence: The body is byte-identical to the ctor pair at 0x002BD834/0x002BD858 and no caller, constructor or vtable slot names it, so the class cannot be inferred from shape.

name: maybe_Save_LoadTask_ResolveObject
signature: void maybe_Save_LoadTask_ResolveObject(void* task, u32 slot, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Looks up the object owning the requested save chunk through the handle table keyed by (f_C >> 12), walks a virtual list to find the matching class, takes two dwords through a virtual call, passes them plus the slot to 0x002CE5A8 and sets the task state to 7.
evidence: The body contains unaff_r5 (damaged decompilation), so the meaning of the resolved pair cannot be settled; only the shape (handle-table lookup, virtual +0x3C, state 7, call to 0x002CE5A8) is readable and the sole caller is Save_Task_DispatchStep.

name: maybe_Ui_Event_WaitSoundThenAdvanceA
summary: Waits for the sound handle at +0x134 to finish and for the save task at +0x13C to complete, then marks +0xD65, notifies save completion, moves the task data and advances the state sequence to 7 or 0xF.
evidence: The recovered body confirms both halves of the name (the sound-handle check through 0x0063071C and the Save_Task_DispatchStep completion), but there are no callers and the state ids 7/0xF are undecoded.

name: maybe_Event_ScriptCommandSaveA
summary: Save-task completion step of an event script command: lazily creates the shared anim-sequence object, checks the sound handle at +0x134, steps the save task at +0x13C, marks +0xD65, notifies save completion and advances the state sequence to 5 or 7.
evidence: The recovered body is the same save-completion sequence as 0x002857D0/0x003B4B44 on a different class (fields +0x13C/+0x14C/+0xD8C), which supports the save-command reading, but there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: maybe_Event_ScriptCommandSaveB
summary: Save-task completion step of an event script command, twin of 0x003B4030: lazily creates the shared anim-sequence object, checks the sound handle at +0x134, steps the save task at +0x13C, marks +0xD65, notifies save completion and advances the state sequence to 5 or 7.
evidence: The recovered body is the same save-completion sequence as 0x003B4030 with different state ids, which supports the save-command reading, but there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Event_AdvanceAfterSaveTask
summary: Steps the save task at +0x13C and, once it completes, marks +0xD65, moves the task data and advances the state sequence to 3 or 0xE depending on the follow-up check.
evidence: The recovered body is a pure Save_Task_DispatchStep completion step, which matches the name; there are no callers and the state ids 3/0xE are undecoded.

name: maybe_Script_Handler_AdvanceAfterSaveTask
summary: Steps the save task at +0x13C and, once it completes, unlinks the +0xD1C node when the child list is empty, marks +0xD65, moves the task data and advances the state sequence to 1 or 6.
evidence: The recovered body is a Save_Task_DispatchStep completion step with an extra child-list unlink, which matches the name; there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: maybe_Script_Handler_AdvanceAfterSaveTaskB
summary: Steps the save task at +0x13C and, once it completes, marks +0xD65, moves the task data and advances the state sequence to 2 or 7.
evidence: The recovered body is the same Save_Task_DispatchStep completion step as 0x003B41C0 without the child-list unlink; there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: Ui_Window_StartSaveSlotTask
summary: Starts a save for the window's current slot: loads the save work data, builds the request record at +0x750 (mode 1, or 2 when the pack-name record's +0x3B byte is clear) and calls Save_SaveTask_StartSlot on the task object at +0x810.
evidence: Both callees are named and specific (Save_LoadWorkData, Save_SaveTask_StartSlot) and the request record is built from the window's own slot index, which pins the start-a-save-slot-task reading.

name: Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroup
signature: void Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroup(void* arg1, void* unit, u32 groupId, void* rows)
summary: Adds a battle unit to one of ten 0x24-byte target-row groups: finds the row keyed by +0x784 (or claims the first 0xFFFF row), stores the unit in the first free of four slots (+0x774..+0x780), adds the unit's HP and MP bar ratios into +0x78C/+0x790 and copies its +0x10 flag into the row's busy byte.
evidence: The two float callees are the named Battle_Monster_GetHpBarRatio / Battle_Monster_GetMpBarRatio and their results are summed into the row fields, and the only caller is Battle_ActionCommand_ProcessSkillEffect, which pins the battle target-row reading.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroupWithValue
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroupWithValue(void* rows, void* unit, u32 groupId, u16 value)
summary: Twin of 0x00279760: inserts a battle unit into the first row whose +0x784 group id matches (or a free 0xFFFF row), accumulates the HP/MP bar ratios and stores a caller-supplied u16 at +0x788 plus the unit flag at +0x794.
evidence: The body is a byte-for-byte copy of the now-confirmed 0x00279760 except the extra strh to +0x788, but its two callers are equip code (Party_EquipItemIntoCategorySlot, maybe_Model_RandomizeEquipSlots), which contradicts the battle-row reading, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Cue_Finish
summary: Checks whether the sound handle at cue+0x10 is stale through Sound_Handle_IsStale; if so it clears the handle and elapsed time and reloads two callback words from the descriptor table.
evidence: Callees Sound_GetPlayer and Sound_Handle_IsStale are named, but there are no callers and no strings, so both 'Cue' and 'Finish' remain inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_InitPartsH
summary: Compact composite destructor/teardown: installs the vtable, tears down the trailing pane chain (inline list unlinks and a 0x38-byte helper object) and finishes with 0x36B514 + 0x1D8C2C + 0x10F6CC.
evidence: There is no caller and no literal; only the shared dtor/table idiom (vtable 0x0036B514, Ui_Object_DtorBase, Ui_LayoutRef_Release) identifies it as a composite-window family member, and the body is a teardown rather than an init.

name: maybe_Ui_SubObject_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the sub-object host: installs the vtable, unlinks the update-list node at self+0x14, releases the owned child through the UI context and releases the host.
evidence: The body carries decompiler damage (extraout_r1 passed to release); the vtable store, the 0x0036B514 unlink and the release order match ctor 0x002D5A08, but no caller or vtable slot names the class.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_CloseByMode
summary: Closes a list window: drains children down to two, unlinks the registered node and selects the embedded element; when mode is 2 it also confirms the current list entry, calls the close observer's +0x10 slot, clears the close flag and hides the cursor icon.
evidence: The recovered body shows the mode==2 close path (Ui_List_ConfirmCurrent, observer +0x10, close flag, cursor hide), which supports the name, but there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_WidgetWith10Rows_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a widget owning ten rows: runs Ui_Object_CtorSmallB, installs the window vtable, initialises the scroller sub-object at +0x54, stores the row count 10 at +0x18 and constructs ten 0x18-byte rows at +0x1C.
evidence: The recovered body shows the explicit row count 10 and std_ConstructArray(..., 0x18, 10), which matches the name, but there are no callers and the class is only known by its vtable constants.

name: maybe_Ui_Element2D_Ctor_vt76007C
summary: Small 0x130-byte 2D UI element constructor: allocates, installs vtable 0x0076007C, sets id -1 and installs the animatable-element base vtable.
evidence: Callers are Ui_TitleScreen_Ctor and Ui_PresentWindow_Ctor, but vtable 0x0076007C carries text-window slots, so the class boundary is not clean enough to rename.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect_ReplaceResource
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Effect_ReplaceResource(void* self, u32* handle, u32 effectId)
summary: Re-points an effect slot at another resource: validates the tagged handle, resolves the owner effect, attaches the new resource and re-applies the sprite pattern.
evidence: Callees Gfx_ResourceList_Attach, Gfx_SpritePane_GetPrimaryMaterial and maybe_Gfx_Sprite_SetupPattern support the replace-and-refresh reading, but the effectId meaning is unconfirmed and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Gfx_ResourceList_PreloadType4
summary: Preloads a batch of 0x25 resources: validates each handle in the request block through the resource table, then attaches each type-4 handle so the assets are resident.
evidence: The loop bound 0x25 and the type-byte 4 checks on handle-table entries followed by Gfx_ResourceList_Attach are visible, but the decompiler artefact unaff_r4 in the second loop keeps it tentative.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect_CreateInstance
summary: Effect-instance helper: runs Gfx_ResourceList_Attach and, when the owner descriptor is non-null, sets up the sprite at owner+0x20.
evidence: The body is damaged (unaff_r4/r7) with only Gfx_ResourceList_Attach and maybe_Gfx_Sprite_SetupPattern visible, and the callee list is an export artefact, so nothing new supports the name.

name: maybe_Actor_SubObject_ResetAndActivate
summary: Resets and activates an actor sub-object: runs Actor_SubObject_Reset, selects the list entry at +0x288, sets bit 0 of +0x44 on every child of +0x180, sets isActive, drains pending children, selects the embedded node, unlinks +0x3430 and restarts the state node at +0x23C.
evidence: The recovered body shows the reset-then-activate sequence with the named Actor_SubObject_Reset callee, which matches the name, but there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetAndActivateB
summary: Resets a UI widget (drains children, unlinks the +0x344C node, runs Actor_SubObject_Reset), lazily creates the shared 0x80-byte state object and returns whether its +0x68 flag pair is fully set, setting bit 1 of +0x6C when it is.
evidence: The recovered body is a reset followed by a shared-state predicate, so 'ResetAndActivate' only describes the first half; there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetB
summary: Teardown of a large UI widget: drains children, unlinks the two intrusive list nodes at +0x344C/+0x34D8, runs the shared base reset and releases the sub-widget at +0xAB8.
evidence: The body drains the child list, unlinks two list nodes and calls Actor_SubObject_Reset and Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub, but there are no callers and the class is still unidentified.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetWithCommand
summary: Reset of a different UI widget class: drains children, unlinks the +0xD36 node, runs the shared base reset, then dispatches virtual command 0x20 with -1 through vtable slot +0x54.
evidence: The body drains children, unlinks f_d36, calls Actor_SubObject_Reset and then makes an indirect call through *self+0x54 with (0x20, -1), but there are no callers and the class is unidentified.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetWithAnim
summary: Resets a UI widget and restarts its pane animation: drains children, unlinks the +0x344C/+0x34D8 nodes, runs Actor_SubObject_Reset, sets bit 0 of +0x44 on every child of +0x1F8, sets the +0x1A8 flag, starts the pane anim frame and restarts the state node at +0x288.
evidence: The recovered body shows the pane-anim start (maybe_Ui_Pane_StartAnimFrame15) plus the child-flag pass, which supports the name, but there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ShowPage9
summary: Switches a window to page 9: drains children down to one, unlinks +0xD36, dispatches virtual command 8 with -1, sets the page byte +0xDE0 to 0xFF, and after checking the first party member's name length sets it to 9 and dispatches virtual +0x58 with that page.
evidence: The recovered body shows the literal page value 9 written to +0xDE0 and dispatched through vtable +0x58, which supports the name, but there are no callers and the class is unproven.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_BuildGlyphBuffers
summary: Fills the message widget's per-line character buffers (full-width at +0xE0, half-width at +0xF4, 32 chars each) from the message records of lineCount lines, stopping at 0xFF markers, and copies the per-line box metrics into +0xB8..+0xDC.
evidence: Both callers are named message-window entry points (Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextById, Ui_FieldScreen_Init) and the callee Ui_Message_SetItemNameArg is a message helper, which pins the message-window glyph-buffer reading; only the lost unaff_r10 keeps the buffer choice partly inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small embedded UI sub-object: stamps the vtable, releases the pane at +0x4C and the list, then frees.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Ui_Screen_Dtor (0x004119E0), which confirms the member-destructor role, but no ctor or vtable sibling proves the concrete 'GuideWindow' class.

name: Field_Placement_GetDefaultArea
summary: Returns the result of 0x00423E94, or the compiled-in default descriptor 0x005A3630 when that returns null; used by the field-placement tests.
evidence: All three callers are field-placement code (Field_Placement_TestAreaA/B, maybe_Ui_TestPlacementFree) and the body is the plain 'query or fall back to the built-in descriptor' shape, which pins the default-area reading.

name: Battle_ActionAnimObject_CtorA
summary: Sub-object constructor for a battle action animation object: calls Battle_ActionSubObject_BaseCtor, installs vtable g_battleActorActionVtableA and zeroes two vector3 fields.
evidence: The only caller is Battle_ActionAnimWindow_Init and the only callee is Battle_ActionSubObject_BaseCtor, both named and specific to the battle action animation window, which pins the class; only the A/B variant distinction is unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_IsPointBehindMove
summary: Returns 1 when the given point lies behind the reference object's last movement: it dots the movement delta (f_bc-f_b0, f_c0-f_b4, f_c4-f_b8) with (point - previous position) and tests < 0.
evidence: Both callers are UI overlay code (Ui_Overlay_UpdateBillboard, Ui_Overlay_UpdateTransform) and the dot product is compared < 0, matching 'behind'; the reference object is (work+8)->f_74, which the established facts identify as the camera child, so the 'Move' wording may really mean the camera's motion.

name: maybe_Ui_Tween_DispatchCommandA
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Tween_DispatchCommandA(void* tween, int opcode, void** targetRef, u32 value)
summary: Opcode dispatcher: 2 runs the step helper, 3 copies the element's current fixed-point values into the target record and reseeds, 4 starts 0x003A6F08 in mode 0; other opcodes hit the trap path.
evidence: The branch condition arrives in a lost flag register (in_ZR) so the body is damaged, and the trap path calls Math_Vector_FixedToFloat with no arguments; there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_Tween_DispatchCommandB
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Tween_DispatchCommandB(void* tween, u32 variant, int opcode, void** targetRef)
summary: Twin opcode dispatcher with the same 2/3/4 handling, but it starts 0x003A6F08 in mode 1 and its trap path calls Math_Vector_FloatToFixed.
evidence: Same damaged in_ZR branch as its twin 0x003A7128; the two trap helpers (FixedToFloat vs FloatToFixed) suggest a pair of inverse opcode tables, but there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_WorldMapMarker_UpdateCurrent
summary: Calls Ui_WorldMapMarker_UpdateVisited and then falls through into the shared highlight loop at 0x003A7F3C, which sets each of 32 markers' visible bit from the save's per-map state byte.
evidence: The 24-byte entry tail-falls into 0x003A7F3C and the loop body belongs to that shared helper, so this is a thin wrapper; there are no callers to confirm the world-map context.

name: maybe_Ui_HighlightList_ApplyMapState
summary: Shared highlight updater: walks 32 8-byte records (element pointer, u16 map id, expected state) and sets bit 0 of element+0x44 when the per-map state byte at bag+0x2A70+mapId equals the record's expected state.
evidence: The callers are unrelated UI list code (Ui_MonsterBook_FillEntry, Ui_NpcIcon_UpdateFromRecord, maybe_Anim2D_RebindRecordTable), so it is a shared record-list helper rather than a world-map method; the name stays layout-descriptive.

name: maybe_Battle_CalcRandomScaleVector
signature: void maybe_Battle_CalcRandomScaleVector(float* out, float* src, float scaleBias)
summary: Writes out[0..2] = src[+0x1C,+0x20,+0x24] * (4.0 + uniform[-0.5,0.5] + scaleBias), then overwrites out[1] with the unscaled src[+0x20]; a small random-jitter scale helper.
evidence: The disassembly shows bl 0x001CA3E4(battleRng+0x4218, 0) with s0=-0.5f/s1=+0.5f and a vadd of 4.0f, so the battle-RNG use is real, but the eight callers are UI/animation scale users, so the 'Battle_' prefix is only supported by the RNG source.

name: maybe_Gfx_BindMaterialSet
signature: void maybe_Gfx_BindMaterialSet(void* context, u32 packetId, u32 variantId)
summary: Resolves the packet handle, asks the context through vtable slot +0x14 for the variant, builds a material set with Gfx_BindResourceSetVariant on the render target at self[2]+0x9C, submits it through 0x0065C1F8 and releases it.
evidence: All callees are named and consistent with a one-shot material-set bind/submit/release, but there are no callers to pin the owning class.

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectNode_AttachTransform
summary: Validates the scene-object handle at +0x220 (type byte 4), finds the expected node class in the owner's node list, attaches it through Gfx_ResourceList_Attach and copies the source node's transform words into the target.
evidence: The old Field_Actor_ prefix was wrong: five of the eight callers are maybe_Gfx_EffectNode_AttachAndApplyA..E and the rest are UI/gold-text code, so this is a shared effect-node attach helper. The attach step is the named Gfx_ResourceList_Attach, but unaff_r5 shows Ghidra lost a register.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_SyncAttachedNodes
summary: Per-frame positioner for 2D nodes/light attached to an object: computes the owner transform (or rotates the local offset by the owner quaternion), writes node positions only when changed, and repeats for every child node.
evidence: The quaternion helpers and child accessors remain unnamed and the function is reached only through a vtable, so the class and verb cannot be pinned.

name: maybe_BattleScene_CheckUnitAbilitiesThumb
signature: u32 maybe_BattleScene_CheckUnitAbilitiesThumb(u32 scene, void* unit, u32 abilityId, u32 ctx)
summary: Thumb implementation of the ability validation loop: walks the unit's ability list and reports whether the requested ability id is present and usable.
evidence: The decompilation carries unaff_r4 and a lost register mapping, so only the loop shape matches BattleScene_CheckUnitAbilities; the only caller is the equally uncertain 0x0060499C.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimSequence_UpdateChildren
signature: void maybe_Ui_AnimSequence_UpdateChildren(void* owner, u32 forwarded, u32 forwarded2)
summary: Drives child animation delegates between self+0x278 and +0x280: on state change it calls their +0x24 reset or +0x28 update virtuals, restarts the current step on child completion and finishes with 0x003F7718.
evidence: Vtable 0x00780A48 slot 0 is this address, but the owner class is unidentified and 0x001BBC0C/0x003F7718 are unnamed, so the animation-sequence reading is still inferred.

name: maybe_BattleScene_CheckUnitAbilitiesC
signature: u32 maybe_BattleScene_CheckUnitAbilitiesC(u32 scene, int index, int entries)
summary: Ability validation loop reading entry ids and querying Pack_HandleChain_IsReleased for each non-0xFFFF ability.
evidence: The body contains unaff_r4..r9 and the only caller (0x001FE184) is unnamed, so the damaged body keeps this at <=0.3.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_UpdateSpeed
summary: Body is damaged: it calls the casino gimmick context installer, then contains a garbled lazy-init of the game work and a float computation stored to self->reelSpinSpeed and work+0x2E1E4.
evidence: Ghidra shows in_fpscr and a bogus lazy-init block, and the two callers (PartyStatus_LoadNewestRecord, Event_ApplyScenarioJumpSettings) are unrelated to the casino; only the callee 0x004AC328 and the work+0x2E1E4 write tie it to the casino family.

name: maybe_Event_Gimmick_UpdateOffset
summary: State-2 update of an event-gimmick offset animation: decays f_38 by 0.8 per call, writes the remaining offset into the sampled node's +0x9C, and once it is <= 0.5 samples the node transform and advances the state byte f_2C to 3.
evidence: Sibling slot 4 (0x004F0EA0) is the state-3 poll of the same f_2C machine and the constants 0x3F4CCCCD (0.8) and ~0.5 are visible, but there are no callers, so the family is inferred from vtable 0x0077C404 neighbours.

name: maybe_Event_Gimmick_UpdateState3
summary: State-3 step of the event-gimmick offset-animation state machine: samples the transform through 0x003DCC3C and advances the state byte f_2C from 3 to 4 once the sampled result code at f_45 reads 3.
evidence: It is a void state-machine step (the callee is called for its side effect on paramState, not for a predicate result), vtable slot 4 of 0x0077C404 next to Event_Gimmick_Constructor, but there are no named callers.

name: maybe_Svc_Cache_BeginWrite
signature: u32 maybe_Svc_Cache_BeginWrite(void* cache, int entryTablePtr, u32 size)
summary: Begins a cache-block write: validates an aligned size in 0x70..0x18000, opens and validates the cache index, records the size and entry-table pointer, and computes the total block size from the directory entries.
evidence: The old Ui_IconCache_ prefix was wrong: the only caller is Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest and the only callee is maybe_Svc_ContentInfo_IsCacheCurrent, both in the Svc/content-cache subsystem, and the body works on a cache file name plus a directory of entries. The cache's concrete owner is still unproven.

name: maybe_Container_HashMap_LookupBySlot
signature: void* maybe_Container_HashMap_LookupBySlot(void* container, u32 ignored, u32 slot)
summary: Looks up the record owning key slot in the two-table container: small-table mode returns the packed word at self+0x21C+slot*4, otherwise it builds the key and linear-probes the buckets at self+0x3CC.
evidence: The callees std_String_InitFrom and 0x00658C38 (bucket key compare) and the two-table layout with slot bounds checks are visible, but the branch condition arrives in a lost flag register (in_ZR) and there are no callers.

name: Battle_Ui_ApplyScrollOffset
signature: void Battle_Ui_ApplyScrollOffset(void* self, float* scroll, u32 arg3, u32 dataKey)
summary: Called from the battle UI scroll-animation update: resolves the character record from the unit's +0x768 id, negates the y scroll component and re-derives the target widget's coordinates from its base values plus the scroll offsets and the record's balloon slot.
evidence: The sole caller is the named Battle_Ui_UpdateScrollAnimation and the body writes target+0x64/+0x68 from f_80/f_84 plus the scroll vector, which pins the scroll-offset application.

name: maybe_std_InitStaticArray
summary: Compiler-generated static initialiser: default-constructs an eight-element array of 4-byte elements from type descriptor 0x005906C0 in a stack buffer; Ghidra marks the constructor non-returning so the rest is unrecoverable.
evidence: The only visible callee is std_ConstructArray with type 0x005906C0, 8 elements of 4 bytes, and the callers are unrelated UI paths, so the static-initialiser reading is still a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_State_Ctor
signature: void maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_State_Ctor(void* state, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructor of a small state block used by the recipe-book/title-demo screens: sets state byte 1, id word -1, two 0xFF sentinels, then constructs three 4-byte elements of type 0x00192580 at +0xA.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_Ctor and the element type 0x00192580 is shared with party-stat code, so the sentinel-init pattern is visible but the class label rests on an unnamed caller.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkDirectionThumbA
signature: void maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkDirectionThumbA(void* grid, void* outCollision, u32 x, u32 y)
summary: Four-byte Thumb entry that falls through into the shared 0x005BEF5A collision-step walker with direction register 0; it walks candidate chips, calls Field2D_MapChip_CheckCollisionStep and copies 0xD-byte step records.
evidence: There are no callers and the decompilation is damaged (unaff_r6/r7/r10, in_stack_* pseudolocals); only the shared walker and Field2D_MapChip_CheckCollisionStep are trustworthy, so the A/B direction split is an interpretation.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkDirectionThumbB
signature: void maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkDirectionThumbB(void* grid, void* outCollision, u32 x, u32 y)
summary: Second four-byte Thumb entry into the same 0x005BEF5A collision-step walker; it walks candidate chips, records collision steps and finishes through the actor's vtable +0x40.
evidence: Same damaged body and the same two named callees as 0x005BEF52; the four bytes of entry code that distinguish A from B are not visible in the C and there is no caller.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdatePathMotion
summary: Advances a gimmick along its path: steps the phase, clamps it against the arc-length table, sets the finished byte, then writes the sampled position/tangent into the caller's frame record.
evidence: Both path readers are now confident (Field_Path_GetPosition, Field_Path_GetTangent) and Math_MatrixInverse is called for the frame, but there is no caller and the sample-write half is still inferred.

name: maybe_Gfx_Trail_ClampProgress
summary: Trail update step: fetches the curve/sample array through the object's vtable +0x70, clamps the two progress floats, writes the clamped progress and rebinds the trail animator.
evidence: The caller is the named Gfx_Trail_UpdateFollowPath, but the body contains bad instruction data, a coprocessor_function pseudo-call and unaff_r5, so the clamping reading is only a hypothesis.

name: maybe_Battle_Actor_SelectStateMessageRow
summary: Selects one of four battle-state ids for the actor's member by priority (0x29/0x2A/0x27/0x28, each tested through virtual +0xE8) and fetches the corresponding data-manager row with 0x0063E05C.
evidence: The body is a priority switch over the four vtable ids plus a 0x0063E05C data-row fetch, but the fetched row may be the return value (Ghidra drops it) and there is no caller, so the name stays tentative.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_InitReelStrip
summary: Constructs a 27-element array of 4-byte elements (element constructor 0x005F9720) in the caller's stack frame; the only caller Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult consumes it as one reel strip.
evidence: The caller is the named Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult, which fixes the casino context, but the function only performs std_ConstructArray(..., 0x005F9720, 4, 0x1B) and reads no reel constant or symbol, so 'reel strip' remains an interpretation.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_InitPaytable
summary: Zeroes a small header with 0xFF sentinels and constructs a three-element array through std_ConstructArray; the body is truncated and reads no paytable constant, so the payout role is unproven.
evidence: The only caller is Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult and the callees include Casino_Slot_PickLosingStop/PickMatchingStop and Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng, but the visible body never dereferences the array and the 912-byte size does not match the few lines shown.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpritePane_FindMaterialValueByName
summary: Looks up a layout object by name through the manager vtable slot +0x2C, verifies it against the sprite-pane vtable and returns the primary material's +0x78 word (0 when absent).
evidence: The caller Ui_PokerWindow_ResolveCardObjects passes a name string and the callee Gfx_SpritePane_GetPrimaryMaterial is named, but what +0x78 means is still unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_WrapRow
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListWindow_WrapRow(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int wrap)
summary: Adds delta to the list's current row index (+0x4C) and, when the result goes negative and wrap is set, wraps it back into range using the item count from vtable +0x64.
evidence: The callers Ui_SakusenWindow_Confirm and Ui_ScrollBar_Update only show cursor movement, and the body ends in three halt_baddata sites plus an indirect call through address 0, so the upper clamp is lost.
